title: Airbrushed Coral Sample Preparation for Isotope Analyses
author: James Price
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgi7juhn

steps.title: Prepare airbrush and coral fragment
steps.instruction: Fill the airbrush reservoir with 15 ml of 0.22 µm filtered ultrapure water; wear nitrile gloves; place a coral fragment (≈2–3 cm² surface area) in a new clean bag.

steps.title: Airbrush coral fragment
steps.instruction: Hold the bag‑opened fragment from outside the bag, airbrush all tissue‑covered surfaces downward into the bag while rotating the fragment as needed; use only as much water as required; note that Poritid corals may require more passes than Pocilloporid corals.

steps.title: Collect and freeze coral slurry
steps.instruction: Open a pre‑labeled 15 ml polypropylene centrifuge tube (Tube A) and pour the slurry from the bag into it; briefly spray the airbrush into the bag to rinse remaining material; leave at least 1 ml headspace and store the tube upright at –80 °C.

steps.title: Defrost slurry and prepare NaCl solution
steps.instruction: Defrost six Tube A samples in a room‑temperature water bath for ~5 min; while defrosting, dissolve 1.4 g NaCl in 40 ml 0.22 µm filtered ultrapure water to make a 35 ppt (3.5 %) NaCl solution, cover and set aside; fill two 250 ml beakers and one 50 ml polypropylene tube with 0.22 µm filtered water; clean the mechanical tissue homogenizer probe by submerging it in each beaker and turning it on for 10 s, then in the 50 ml tube, replacing the water in the 50 ml tube between each sample.

steps.title: Homogenize slurry and subsample
steps.instruction: After defrosting, turn on the cleaned homogenizer and homogenize each 15 ml Tube A slurry for 10 s, avoiding blade‑tube contact; using a Pasteur pipette transfer 3 ml of slurry to a new tube (Tube B); store the remaining original slurry at –80 °C; repeat for all six samples; if the slurry is very dilute, a larger subsample may be needed to obtain ~500 µg C and 50 µg N.

steps.title: Further homogenize and sonicate subsample
steps.instruction: Homogenize each 3 ml Tube B subsample with the cleaned tissue tearor for 50 s, avoiding blade contact; move the tube to the sonicator and position the probe ~2 cm below the meniscus; sonicate for 60 s at 20 % amplitude with 1 s pulses; clean the sonicator probe with filtered water and a tissue wipe before proceeding to the next sample.

steps.title: Centrifuge to obtain host supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge each 3 ml Tube B at 500 × g for 2.5 min; using a glass Pasteur pipette carefully transfer the supernatant (host fraction) to a labeled Tube C, avoiding the algal pellet; store Tube C at –80 °C; exact volume is not critical.

steps.title: Wash algal pellet with NaCl
steps.instruction: To each Tube B containing the algal pellet, add ~3 ml of the 35 ppt NaCl solution, vortex 10 s, centrifuge at 400 × g for 2 min, and discard the supernatant; repeat the wash once more to remove residual host tissue; retain the small pellet of algal cells (and a bit of skeleton).

steps.title: Assemble and rinse nylon mesh filter
steps.instruction: Prepare the mesh filter assembly with two 5 cm × 5 cm pieces of 20 µm nylon mesh offset 45°; place the assembly in a side‑arm vacuum flask above an unlabeled 50 ml polypropylene “rinse tube”; turn on the vacuum pump and rinse the mesh with 3 ml filtered water using a Pasteur pipette, then turn off the vacuum and discard the rinse water.

steps.title: Filter algal pellet through mesh
steps.instruction: Replace the rinse tube with a fresh 50 ml tube (Tube D) for the sample; add 5 ml filtered water to the algal pellet in Tube B, cap and vortex 10 s; turn on a suitable vacuum source; transfer the contents of Tube B to the mesh filter assembly with a Pasteur pipette and filter; rinse the mesh with ≥10 ml filtered water until the filtrate appears clear; collect the filtrate in Tube D, cap, and store at 4 °C; after each sample discard and replace the mesh and clean the apparatus in a filtered water bath.

steps.title: Collect algal fraction on glass fiber filter
steps.instruction: Set up a glass fiber filter (GF/F) on the frit of a filter assembly and clip a 15 ml funnel on top; turn on the vacuum (six‑port or single); vortex Tube D 10 s and transfer all algal filtrate to the GF/F using a Pasteur pipette; allow a dark green/brown layer to form; if the filter clogs, increase vacuum strength or hand‑cover the funnel; turn off vacuum when filtration is complete; repeat for all samples.

steps.title: Acidify algal filter to remove skeleton
steps.instruction: With the vacuum off and the silicone stopper seal broken, place four drops of 10 % HCl onto the algal material on the GF/F; let sit 30 s; reopen the vacuum and rinse the filter with 5 ml filtered water using a new Pasteur pipette; repeat for each sample; after rinsing, turn off vacuum and break the seal again.

steps.title: Dry algal fraction on aluminum pan
steps.instruction: Using tweezers cleaned with 70 % isopropyl alcohol between samples, transfer each filter with algal residue onto a pre‑baked, labeled aluminum pan; place the pans in a drying oven set to 60 °C and dry overnight; repeat for all samples.

steps.title: Prepare host fraction for drying
steps.instruction: Defrost the required Tube C samples (typically 20–30) in a room‑temperature water bath; while thawing, set up a clear plastic box and drying station in a fume hood and connect argon gas; after thawing, vortex each Tube C 10 s and centrifuge at 2,000 × g for 5 min to pellet any remaining algal cells.

steps.title: Set up tin capsule doublets
steps.instruction: Clean the tabletop and tape clean aluminum foil where samples will be folded; using forceps, prepare 9 mm × 10 mm tin capsule doublets (inner capsule placed inside outer capsule, outer flared); weigh each doublet and record its weight and rack position on a data sheet; place doublets in alternating openings of a microcentrifuge tube rack.

steps.title: Dry host fraction into tin capsules
steps.instruction: Turn on the hot plate inside the plastic box and set to approximately 90 °C; after centrifugation, transfer ~0.25 ml of host supernatant into each pre‑weighed tin doublet with a Pasteur pipette; add the sample ID to the data sheet; place the doublets under glass pipettes blowing argon gas; if more samples than pipettes, rotate the doublets every 15–20 min; allow the host fraction to dry (~2 h) until ~1.5 mg dried tissue (≈500 µg C, 50 µg N) is obtained; re‑weigh the doublets.

steps.title: Fold and store host tin capsules
steps.instruction: Clean the folding setup (aluminum foil, tweezers, folding block) with a 70 % isopropyl alcohol swab between samples; using two pairs of forceps, press the inner capsule closed and fold it over itself on the block; flatten the outer capsule, then fold into a “Z” shape, flatten, fold into an opposite “Z”, flatten; compress the capsule to eliminate air and sharp corners; place each folded capsule into a 96‑well polypropylene plate, recording the well position; store the plate in a desiccator cabinet (or at –80 °C if storage exceeds one week).

steps.title: Fold and store algal tin capsules
steps.instruction: Clean the folding setup (aluminum foil, tweezers, razor blade, folding block) with alcohol between samples; place the dried algal filter on weighing paper; in the folding block, flare a 3.5 mm × 5 mm tin capsule; cut the filter in half with the razor; using tweezers, scrape the dried algae off each half at a 45° angle into the capsule; close the capsule with tweezers and flatten; perform the same “Z” folding sequence as for the host capsules, compress, and place the capsules into a 96‑well plate, recording well positions; store the plate in a desiccator cabinet or at –80 °C for longer periods.

steps.title: Prepare for isotopic analysis
steps.instruction: Load the compressed host and algal tin capsules into an elemental analyzer coupled to a stable isotope ratio mass spectrometer; run 10 % of all samples in duplicate to assess preparation error; include periodic blanks (water only) to monitor contamination.
